$comment: L2 gloss layer for the ingested Texas clauses: plain-language 'what this means' rewrites at two reading levels (src/schema/gloss.ts). Batch-drafted, then frozen; reviewed_by records the initial editorial pass — a named human reviewer should confirm each gloss against the clause text before classroom use. Reading levels are enforced by scripts/check-reading-level.mjs. A gloss explains only its own clause: it never imports rules from neighboring sections, even when the neighbor is what makes the clause interesting.

glosses.grade_5: Texas has nine judges on its top court. Voters choose them at an election. Each one serves six years. A judge must be 35 or older and must have worked in law for ten years.
glosses.grade_8: The Texas Supreme Court has a Chief Justice and eight Justices. Voters elect them to six-year terms, three seats every two years. A Justice must be at least 35, licensed to practice law in Texas, and must have ten years of work as a lawyer or judge.

glosses.grade_5: Texas lets each school district raise its own tax money for its own schools. But first the voters who live there must say yes to the tax.
glosses.grade_8: This section lets the Legislature form school districts and lets those districts levy a local property tax to run their schools and put up school buildings. The tax takes effect only if most of the district's voters approve it at an election.

glosses.grade_5: The state of Texas may not tax land or buildings. One short line is the whole rule.
glosses.grade_8: Texas may not levy a statewide ad valorem tax, which is a tax on the value of property. The ban is on the State itself, and this section says nothing about taxes levied by local governments.
